tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains:
questions.topic: Uniform Circular Motion - Velocity and Acceleration
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the direction of velocity changes continuously even though speed is constant, so velocity is not constant. Centripetal acceleration's direction also keeps changing (always pointing toward center), so acceleration is also not constant - both velocity and acceleration vary in direction.

questions.text: Two students performed the same experiment separately and each one of them recorded two readings of mass which are given below. Correct result for the experiment is known to be 3.0 g. Student A: 3.01 g, 2.99 g. Student B: 3.05 g, 2.95 g. On the basis of given data, mark the correct statement.
options: Results of both students are neither accurate nor precise.
Results of student A are both precise and accurate.
Results of student B are neither precise nor accurate.
Results of student B are both precise and accurate.
questions.explanation: Student A's readings (3.01, 2.99) are close to each other (precise) and their average (3.00) matches the correct value (accurate). So A's results are both precise and accurate; B's readings are more scattered, hence less precise.

questions.text: Naked cytoplasm, multinucleated, and saprophytic are the characteristics of
questions.explanation: Slime molds exhibit a naked multinucleate mass of protoplasm (plasmodium) during their feeding stage and are saprophytic, feeding on decaying organic matter.

questions.text: Ka1, Ka2 and Ka3 are the respective ionisation constants for the following reactions: H2S ⇌ H+ + HS−; HS− ⇌ H+ + S²−; H2S ⇌ 2H+ + S²−. The correct relationship between Ka1, Ka2 and Ka3 is
questions.explanation: Adding the two stepwise reactions gives the overall reaction, so the overall equilibrium constant is the product of the stepwise constants: Ka3 = Ka1 × Ka2.

questions.text: A point object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a convex lens of focal length 30 cm. If a plane mirror were put perpendicular to the principal axis of the lens and at a distance of 40 cm from it, the final image would be formed at a distance of:
options: 20 cm from the lens, it would be a real image
30 cm from the lens, it would be a real image
30 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image
20 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image
questions.topic: Image formation with lens and plane mirror
questions.explanation: First refraction: 1/v-1/(-60)=1/30 → v=60cm (beyond the mirror at 40cm, so mirror intercepts converging rays), forming a virtual object for the mirror which reflects to form a real image 20cm in front of mirror, i.e., 20cm from the lens.

questions.text: A hollow metal sphere of radius R is uniformly charged. The electric field due to the sphere at a distance r from the centre:
options: Zero as r increases from r < R increases as r increases for r > R
decreases as r increases for r < R and for r > R
increases as r increases for r < R and for r > R
zero as r increases for r < R, decreases as r increases for r > R
questions.topic: Electric Field due to Charged Sphere
questions.explanation: For a hollow charged sphere, inside the sphere (r<R) the electric field is zero everywhere (no charge enclosed). Outside the sphere (r>R), field E=kQ/r^2, which decreases as r increases.

questions.text: A wire of length L, area of cross section A is hanging from a fixed support. The length of the wire changes to L1 when mass M is suspended from its free end. The expression for Young's modulus is:
questions.explanation: Young's modulus Y = (Stress)/(Strain) = (Mg/A)/((L1-L)/L) = MgL/(A(L1-L)).

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) 6-15 pairs of gill slits, (b) Heterocercal caudal fin, (c) Air Bladder, (d) Poison sting with (i) Trygon, (ii) Cyclostomes, (iii) Chondrichthyes, (iv) Osteichthyes
questions.topic: Classification of fish and chordate features
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes have 6-15 pairs of gill slits (ii), Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish, e.g. sharks) have a heterocercal caudal fin (iii), Osteichthyes (bony fish) have an air bladder (iv), and Trygon (a stingray) has a poison sting (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, T(K): ln k=14.34-1.25×10⁴/T. The energy of activation in kcal mol⁻¹ for the reaction is: (k in s⁻¹, R=1.987 cal mol⁻¹K⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Comparing with ln k = ln A - Ea/RT, Ea/R=1.25×10⁴ → Ea=1.25×10⁴×1.987 cal/mol ≈ 24840 cal/mol = 24.84 kcal/mol.

questions.text: An ac circuit contains a resistance of 1 kΩ, a capacitor of 0.1 μF and an inductor of 1 mH connected in series. The resonance frequency of the circuit is approximately:
Which one of the following alcoholic drinks is produced without distillation?
questions.explanation: Wine is produced simply by fermentation of fruit juice (such as grape juice) without any distillation step, unlike whisky, rum, and brandy, which are all distilled spirits.

questions.text: Match List I with List II with respect to chronology of evolution of life forms: List I — A. About 65 mya, B. About 500 mya, C. About 350 mya, D. About 320 mya. List II — I. Jawless fish probably evolved, II. The dinosaurs suddenly disappeared from the earth, III. Seaweeds and few plants probably existed, IV. Invertebrates were formed and became active.
questions.topic: Matching evolutionary chronology of life forms
questions.explanation: About 65 mya dinosaurs disappeared (II); about 500 mya jawless fish evolved (I); about 350 mya seaweeds/plants existed (III); about 320 mya invertebrates became active (IV). A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur: (1) CuSO4(aq) + Zn(s) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s) (2) CuSO4(aq) + Fe(s) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s) (3) FeSO4(aq) + Zn(s) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s) (4) 2CuSO4(aq) + 2Ag(s) -> 2Cu(s) + Ag2SO4(aq)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 would require Ag (E=0.80V, a weaker reducing agent) to reduce Cu2+ (E=0.34V), but since Ag has a higher (more positive) reduction potential than Cu, Ag will not spontaneously reduce Cu2+ ions; rather the reverse would occur. So this reaction cannot occur spontaneously.

questions.text: The chances of contracting bird flu from a properly cooked (above 100°C) chicken or egg are
questions.topic: Bird Flu and Properly Cooked Poultry
questions.explanation: The bird flu (avian influenza) virus is inactivated by heat; thoroughly cooking chicken or eggs above 100°C destroys the virus, eliminating the risk of transmission.

questions.text: The biodegradable polymer is:
questions.explanation: Nylon-2-nylon-6 is a biodegradable polymer because it contains amide linkages similar to proteins/peptides, which can be broken down by biological processes, unlike nylon-6, nylon-6,6, or Buna-S (a synthetic rubber), which are non-biodegradable.

questions.text: The effective resistance of a parallel connection that consists of four wires of equal length, equal area of cross-section and same material is 0.25 Ω. What will be the effective resistance if they are connected in series?
questions.explanation: If R is resistance of each wire, parallel: R/4=0.25 → R=1Ω. Series: 4R=4Ω.

questions.text: The reaction that does NOT take place in a blast furnace between 900 K to 1500 K temperature range during extraction of iron is:
questions.explanation: The reaction Fe2O3 + CO -> 2FeO + CO2 occurs at a lower temperature range (around 500-800 K) in the blast furnace, not in the 900 K to 1500 K range. The reactions FeO + CO -> Fe + CO2, C + CO2 -> 2CO, and CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3 all occur within the 900 K to 1500 K range.

questions.text: Which of the following hormones can play a significant role in osteoporosis?
questions.explanation: Estrogen deficiency (common after menopause) and parathyroid hormone imbalance (which regulates calcium mobilisation from bone) are both significantly linked to the development of osteoporosis.

questions.text: In a qualitative analysis, Bi³⁺ is detected by appearance of precipitate BiO(OH)(s). Calculate the pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298K: BiO(OH)(s)⇌BiO⁺(aq)+OH⁻(aq), K=4×10⁻¹⁰ (Given: log2=0.3010)
The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is:
questions.topic: Fundamental Frequency - Open vs Closed Pipe
questions.explanation: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f0 = v/2l. For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency fc = v/4l. The ratio f0:fc = (v/2l):(v/4l) = 2:1.

tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A rectangular film of liquid is extended from (4cm × 2cm) to (5cm × 4cm). If the work done is 3×10⁻⁴ J, the value of the surface tension of the liquid is:
questions.explanation: Work done W = 2TΔA (factor of 2 for two surfaces of the film). ΔA = (5×4 - 4×2) cm² = (20-8) cm² = 12 cm² = 12×10⁻⁴ m². So 3×10⁻⁴ = 2×T×12×10⁻⁴, giving T = 3/24 = 0.125 N/m.

questions.text: A body of mass 2kg travels according to the law x(t) = pt + qt² + rt³ where p = 3m s⁻¹, q = 4m s⁻², and r = 5m s⁻³. The force acting on the body at t = 2 seconds is
Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
questions.explanation: Phellem (cork), produced by the cork cambium, is made up of dead cells with suberin deposited in their walls, making them impervious to water and gases.

questions.text: The relation between acceleration and displacement of four particles are given below: Which one executes SHM?
questions.explanation: SHM requires acceleration directly proportional to displacement but oppositely directed: a = -ω²x. Only a = -2x fits this linear, restoring-force form (ω² = 2); the others are either not linear in x or not restoring.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Photovoltaic device can convert optical radiation into electricity.
Statement II: Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic devices (solar cells) do convert optical radiation into electrical energy, and Zener diodes are indeed specifically designed to operate in reverse bias breakdown region for voltage regulation applications. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: The difference between amylose and amylopectin is
options: Amylose is made up of glucose and galactose
questions.explanation: Amylopectin is a branched polysaccharide of glucose units joined by α-1,4 glycosidic linkages along the chain and α-1,6 glycosidic linkages at the branch points.

questions.text: Gadolinium has a low value of third ionisation enthalpy because of:
questions.explanation: Gadolinium has configuration [Xe]4f7 5d1 6s2. Removing the third electron gives Gd3+ with [Xe]4f7, a stable half-filled f-subshell configuration, which has high exchange energy, making the third ionisation comparatively easier (lower ionisation enthalpy).

questions.text: Two point charges A and B, having charges +Q and -Q respectively, are placed at a certain distance apart and the force acting between them is F. If 25% charge of A is transferred to B, then the force between the charges becomes:
questions.explanation: Originally F = kQ^2/d^2. After transfer, charge on A becomes (3/4)Q and on B becomes -Q-(1/4)Q = -(5/4)Q... Actually per the solution: new charges are (3/4)Q and -(3/4)Q, so F' = k(9/16)Q^2/d^2 = (9/16)F.

questions.text: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchical arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The correct taxonomic hierarchy in descending order (which the question calls ascending, as officially keyed) is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - nitro group is electron withdrawing, increasing acidic strength of nitrophenol compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol do NOT have the same acidic strength; they differ due to differences in resonance and inductive effects based on position (order: p-nitrophenol > o-nitrophenol > m-nitrophenol in Ka, though exact order can vary by effect considered).

questions.text: The percentage of pyridine (C5H5N) that forms pyridinium ion (C5H5N+H) in a 0.10 M aqueous pyridine solution (Kb for C5H5N = 1.7×10^-9) is:

A sheet is placed on a horizontal surface in front of a strong magnetic pole. A force is needed to:
A. hold the sheet there if it is magnetic.
B. hold the sheet there if it is non-magnetic.
C. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is conducting.
D. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is both, non-conducting and non-polar.
Choose the correct statements(s) from the options given below:
questions.topic: Eddy Currents - Force on Sheet Near Magnetic Pole
questions.explanation: A force is needed to hold a magnetic sheet in place since it is attracted to the pole (A, true). Moving a conducting sheet with uniform velocity away from the pole requires force to overcome the opposing force from induced eddy currents (C, true). A non-magnetic sheet needs no holding force (B, false), and a non-conducting, non-polar (non-magnetic) sheet needs no force to move since no eddy currents or magnetic force act on it (D, false). So A and C only.

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Ion): A. Co2+, B. Mg2+, C. Pb2+, D. Al3+. List II (Group Number in Cation Analysis): I. Group-I, II. Group-III, III. Group-IV, IV. Group-VI. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Co2+ is in Group-IV (Mn2+, Co2+, Zn2+, Ni2+), Mg2+ is in Group-VI, Pb2+ is in Group-I (Ag+, Hg2²+, Pb2+), Al3+ is in Group-III (Fe3+, Cr3+, Al3+). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyze the following reaction: S-G + S# → S + S#-G. Where, G → a group other than hydrogen, S → a substrate, S# → another substrate
questions.explanation: This reaction shows transfer of a group (G, other than hydrogen) from one substrate to another, which is catalyzed by transferase enzymes.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistance P and Q:
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum precision in a Wheatstone bridge, resistances P and Q should be approximately equal (and small), as this minimizes the experimental error.

questions.text: Which of the following is true for nucleolus?
options: Larger nucleoli are present in dividing cells.
It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
It takes part in spindle formation.
questions.topic: Structure and function of the nucleolus
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and assembly of ribosomal subunits; it is a non-membrane-bound structure and is typically larger in metabolically active (non-dividing, protein-synthesizing) cells.

questions.text: Identify the suitable reagent for the following conversion: Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) to benzaldehyde (PhCHO).
questions.topic: Partial Reduction of Esters to Aldehydes
questions.explanation: DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) is a mild reducing agent that partially reduces esters to aldehydes at low temperature, stopping at the aldehyde stage before over-reduction to alcohol. LiAlH4 would over-reduce the ester all the way to the alcohol.

questions.text: Red List contains data or information on:
options: plants whose products are in international trade
questions.explanation: The IUCN Red List contains data on threatened species (plants and animals facing risk of extinction)

questions.text: The C-peptide of human insulin is
options: a part of the mature insulin molecule.
responsible for the formation of disulphide bridges.
removed during the maturation of pro-insulin to insulin.
questions.topic: Role of C-peptide in Insulin Maturation
questions.explanation: Pro-insulin contains an extra connecting (C) peptide linking the A and B chains; this C-peptide is enzymatically removed during the maturation process, leaving the mature, biologically active insulin molecule.

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is not an aromatic compound? (1) Cycloheptatrienyl cation (tropylium cation, planar, 6 pi electrons) (2) Cyclopropenyl cation (planar, 2 pi electrons) (3) Cycloheptatriene with an exocyclic sp3 carbon bearing a positive charge substituent (non-planar at that carbon) (4) Cyclopentadienyl anion (planar, 6 pi electrons)
options: Compound with sp3 hybridized carbon bearing substituent, making ring non-planar
questions.explanation: The compound in option 3 has an sp3 hybridized carbon in the ring (not fully conjugated/planar), so it is cyclic but not planar, and therefore cannot be aromatic despite being cyclic. The other three (tropylium cation, cyclopropenyl cation, cyclopentadienyl anion) are all planar, cyclic, conjugated systems following Huckel's rule and are aromatic.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 11 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about glucose?
options: On heating with HI, it forms n-hexane.
It is present in furanose form.
It does not give the 2,4-DNP test.
questions.explanation: Glucose exists predominantly in the six-membered pyranose ring form (not furanose, which is the five-membered ring typical of fructose or ribose), making this statement false. The other three statements are all true of glucose: it is an aldohexose, HI reduction of its backbone gives n-hexane, and since it does have a free aldehyde group, it actually DOES give a positive 2,4-DNP test — meaning that particular statement, taken as worded ('does not give'), is also false, but the originally intended NCERT answer is the furanose-form statement.

questions.text: Match the following with respect to meiosis: (a) Zygotene, (b) Pachytene, (c) Diplotene, (d) Diakinesis with (i) Terminalization, (ii) Chiasmata, (iii) Crossing over, (iv) Synapsis
questions.explanation: Zygotene is characterised by synapsis (pairing of homologous chromosomes) (iv), Pachytene involves crossing over (iii), Diplotene shows chiasmata (ii), and Diakinesis is marked by terminalization of chiasmata (i). This matches a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: 4 L of 0.02 M aqueous NaCl solution was diluted by adding 1 L of water. The concentration of the resultant solution is
questions.topic: Concentration After Dilution of a NaCl Solution
questions.explanation: Using M1V1 = M2V2 for dilution: (0.02 M)(4 L) = M2(5 L), so M2 = 0.08/5 = 0.016 M. The moles of NaCl (0.08 mol) stay constant while the total volume increases from 4 L to 5 L.

questions.text: A gas is allowed to expand in a well insulated container against a constant external pressure of 2.5 atm from an initial volume of 2.50 L to a final volume of 4.50 L. The change in internal energy delta-U of the gas in joules will be:
questions.topic: Work done and change in internal energy
questions.explanation: For an insulated (adiabatic, q=0) container, delta-U = -W = -P_ext x delta-V = -2.5 atm x (4.50-2.50) L = -5 L.atm. Converting: -5 x 101.325 J = -506.6 J, approximately -505 J.

questions.text: Consider the following nuclear reaction: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + ⁴He. Take masses of ²³⁸U, ²³⁴Th and ⁴He as 238.050 u, 234.043 u and 4.003 u, respectively. The Q value for the reaction, in keV, is: [Given: 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²]
The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of 1000 kg to a height of 20 m in 10 s is: (g=9.8 m/s²)

Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone (pentan-2-one) in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? [This is a crossed aldol condensation question with four structurally drawn options representing different possible condensation products]
options: A cross-aldol condensation product with a chlorine substituent and specific branching pattern derived from a pentan-3-one-like substrate (not the actual substrate used)
A valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
questions.explanation: This is an aldol condensation reaction between acetone and pentan-2-one. Option (1) shows a product structure that would only form if pentan-3-one were the substrate, but the actual substrates are pentan-2-one and acetone, so option (1) cannot be formed from this reaction.

questions.text: In a vernier calliper, 20 VSD coincide with 16 MSD (each division of length 1 mm). The least count of the vernier calliper is:
questions.explanation: 1 VSD=16/20 MSD=0.8mm. Least count=1MSD-1VSD=1-0.8=0.2mm=0.02 cm.

questions.text: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is:
questions.topic: Pitch of a screw gauge from least count and divisions
questions.explanation: Pitch = Least count × number of divisions on circular scale = 0.01×50 = 0.5 mm.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is not true about classical smog?
options: Its main components are produced by the action of sunlight on automobile or factory emissions.
It is produced in cold and humid climate.
It contains compounds of a reducing nature.
It contains smoke, fog and sulphur dioxide.
questions.explanation: Classical (London-type) smog forms from the reaction of smoke, fog, and SO2 in cold, humid weather, and does not require sunlight. The description of sunlight acting on emissions actually applies to photochemical smog, not classical smog.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs
List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Li-electrochemical cells(ii), Na-coolant in fast breeder reactors(iii), KOH-absorbent for CO2(i), Cs-photoelectric cell(iv). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(iv).

questions.text: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0–10 A. The shunt required is:

Match List I (Cells) with List II (Secretion): A. Peptic cells, B. Goblet Cells, C. Oxyntic cells, D. Hepatic cells. List II: I. Mucus, II. Bile juice, III. Proenzyme pepsinogen, IV. HCl and intrinsic factor for absorption of vitamin B12. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.topic: Gastric Gland Cell Types and Secretions
questions.explanation: Peptic (chief) cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen (A-III). Goblet cells secrete mucus (B-I). Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption (C-IV). Hepatic cells secrete bile juice (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Three resistors having resistances r1, r2 and r3 are connected as shown in the given circuit. The ratio i3/i1 of currents in terms of resistances used in the circuit is:
questions.topic: Ratio of currents in a Wheatstone-bridge-like circuit
questions.explanation: By current division at the junction between the parallel branches r2 and r3, i3/i1 (total current split) = r2/(r2+r3).

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field E in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and the area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is: (ε₀ = permittivity of free space)
questions.topic: Energy Stored in Parallel Plate Capacitor from Field
questions.explanation: Energy stored = Energy density × volume = (1/2)ε₀E² × (Ad) = (1/2)ε₀E²Ad.

questions.text: Which of the following features of genetic code does allow bacteria to produce human insulin by recombinant DNA technology?
questions.explanation: The near universality of the genetic code (being essentially the same across organisms) allows bacteria to correctly translate the human insulin gene into functional insulin protein.

questions.text: Which of the carbonates given below is unstable in air and is kept in a CO2 atmosphere to avoid decomposition?
questions.explanation: BeCO3 is highly unstable due to the very high polarising power of the small Be2+ ion, and must be stored under a CO2 atmosphere to prevent its decomposition.

questions.text: A prothallus is
options: a structure in pteridophytes formed before the thallus develops.
a sporophytic free-living structure formed in pteridophytes.
a gametophytic free-living structure formed in pteridophytes.
a primitive structure formed after fertilisation in pteridophytes.
questions.explanation: The prothallus is the small, free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte generation of pteridophytes (ferns), developing from a germinated spore before producing gametes.

questions.text: The promoter site and the terminator site for transcription are located at the
questions.topic: Location of Promoter and Terminator in Transcription
questions.explanation: The promoter, which RNA polymerase binds to initiate transcription, lies upstream (towards the 5' end) of the gene, while the terminator, which signals the end of transcription, lies downstream (towards the 3' end).

questions.text: Variations arising during mutations and meiotic recombinations are
questions.topic: Nature of Mutational and Recombinational Variation
questions.explanation: Mutations and recombinations introduce variation randomly, with no inherent direction or bias toward being advantageous; it is natural selection acting afterward on this random variation that produces directional change in a population.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 12 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: In context with beryllium, which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Its hydride is electron-deficient and polymeric.
It is rendered passive by nitric acid.
questions.explanation: Beryllium salts actually hydrolyze readily (due to high charge density of Be2+), not rarely, making statement (4) incorrect.

questions.text: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are:
questions.explanation: Random errors arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in experimental conditions like temperature, voltage supply, and other environmental factors, and cannot be eliminated completely but can be minimized by taking multiple readings.

questions.text: The pressure of a 1:4 mixture of dihydrogen and dioxygen enclosed in a vessel is one atmosphere. What would be the partial pressure of dioxygen?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction of O2 = 4/5 = 0.8. Partial pressure of O2 = 0.8 × 1 atm = 0.8 atm ≈ 0.8 × 1.013×10⁵ Pa ≈ 8×10⁴ Nm⁻².

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause for loss of biodiversity?
questions.explanation: Keeping animals in zoological parks is generally a conservation measure (ex-situ conservation), not a cause of biodiversity loss, unlike habitat destruction, invasive species, and over-exploitation.

questions.text: In total internal reflection when the angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle for the pair of media in contact, what will be the angle of refraction?
questions.explanation: At the critical angle, the refracted ray grazes along the interface, meaning the angle of refraction becomes 90 degrees (angle of incidence = critical angle implies angle of refraction = 90 degrees).

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30 degrees and 45 degrees with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity equals the slope of the displacement-time graph, i.e., tan(theta). v1:v2 = tan30:tan45 = (1/sqrt3):1 = 1:sqrt(3).

questions.text: The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from 600 rpm to 1200 rpm in 10 s. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is:
questions.explanation: Average ω=(600+1200)/2=900 rpm = 15 rev/s; in 10s → 150 revolutions.

questions.text: Methanogenic bacteria are NOT found in
options: the bottom of water-logged paddy fields.
questions.explanation: Methanogens are strictly anaerobic and thrive in oxygen-free environments such as the cattle rumen, gobar gas plants, and waterlogged paddy field sediments; activated sludge, used in aerobic sewage treatment, is an oxygen-rich environment unsuitable for methanogens.

questions.text: The commercial name of polyacrylonitrile is
questions.explanation: Polyacrylonitrile, formed by the addition polymerisation of acrylonitrile (CH2=CH-CN), is sold commercially as Orlon (also known as acrilan), widely used as a synthetic fibre.

questions.text: Ten E.coli cells with 15N-dsDNA are incubated in medium containing 14N nucleotide. After 60 minutes, how many E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from 15N?
questions.explanation: Assuming a generation time of 20 minutes, after 60 minutes (3 generations), starting from 10 cells, DNA completely free of 15N would be found in 60 cells (semi-conservative replication pattern after 3 divisions).

questions.text: Respiration in insects is called direct because
options: the cells exchange O2/CO2 directly with the air in the tracheal tubes.
the tissues exchange O2/CO2 directly with the coelomic fluid.
the tissues exchange O2/CO2 directly with the air outside through the body surface.
tracheal tubes exchange O2/CO2 directly with the haemocoel, which then exchanges with tissues.
questions.explanation: In insects, the tracheal system delivers air directly to individual cells/tissues through branching tracheal tubes, bypassing the circulatory system entirely — making gas exchange 'direct'.

questions.text: Which will make a basic buffer?
options: 100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 200 mL of 0.1 M NH4OH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH + 25 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH
100 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
questions.explanation: Mixing HCl with excess NH4OH (weak base): HCl + NH4OH -> NH4Cl + H2O. With 0.01 mol HCl and 0.02 mol NH4OH, after reaction 0.01 mol NH4OH remains along with 0.01 mol NH4Cl formed, creating a buffer of weak base NH4OH and its conjugate acid salt NH4Cl, which is a basic buffer.

questions.text: Two atoms are said to be isobars if
options: they have same atomic number but different mass number.
they have same number of electrons but different number of neutrons.
they have same number of neutrons but different number of electrons.
sum of the number of protons and neutrons is same but the number of protons is different.
questions.explanation: Isobars are atoms of different elements (different atomic number/protons) that have the same mass number — i.e., the sum of protons and neutrons is the same, but the number of protons differs.

questions.text: A 40 μF capacitor is connected to a 200 V, 50 Hz ac supply. The rms value of the current in the circuit is, nearly:
questions.topic: RMS current through a capacitor in an AC circuit

questions.text: Which one of the following nitro-compounds does not react with nitrous acid? Options: (1) 3-methyl-2-nitrobutan... (with alpha H) (2) a nitro compound with CH2 alpha carbon (3) a nitro compound with CH alpha carbon (4) 2-methyl-2-nitropropane ((CH3)3C-NO2, no alpha H)
options: Nitro compound with a ketone and alpha-CH
Primary nitroalkane with CH2 alpha carbon
Secondary nitroalkane with CH alpha carbon
questions.explanation: (CH3)3C-NO2 is a tertiary nitro compound with no alpha-hydrogen, so it cannot react with nitrous acid (which requires an alpha-H for the reaction to proceed), unlike primary and secondary nitroalkanes.

questions.text: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm, when it delivers the power of 3.3×10⁻³ watt will be: (h=6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js)
questions.topic: Photons per second emitted by a source
questions.explanation: Energy per photon=hc/λ=(6.6×10⁻³⁴×3×10⁸)/(600×10⁻⁹)≈3.3×10⁻¹⁹ J. Photons/s=3.3×10⁻³/3.3×10⁻¹⁹=10¹⁶.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. CH3-CH-CH3→OH (acid conditions), B. CH3COOH→CH3CH2OH, C. CH3CH2OH→CH3-CH=CH-OH, D. [cyclohexanol derivative]→OH. List II — I. (i) oleum, (ii) H+, II. (i) O2, (ii) H2O/H+, III. (i) CH3OH, H+, (ii) H2, catalyst, IV. (i) conc. H2SO4, (ii) H+/H2O.
questions.explanation: Per official key, correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The primary CO2 acceptor in C4 plants is phosphoenolpyruvate and is found in the mesophyll cells. Statement II: Mesophyll cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCo enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: in C4 plants, PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) is the primary CO2 acceptor present in mesophyll cells (catalyzed by PEP carboxylase), and RuBisCo is absent from mesophyll cells, being present only in bundle sheath cells.

questions.text: Two point charges −q and +q are placed at a distance of L, as shown in the figure. The magnitude of electric field intensity at a distance R (R>>L) varies as:
questions.explanation: Since R>>L, the charge system acts as an electric dipole. Electric field on the axis of a dipole is E = 2kP/R³, so E ∝ 1/R³.

questions.text: If '8' Drosophila in laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is ___________ individuals per Drosophila per week.
questions.explanation: Death rate = number of deaths/original population = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 83)

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 13 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is -3.4 eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately: (1eV=1.6×10⁻¹⁹J, e=1.6×10⁻¹⁹C, 1/4πε0=9×10⁹ Nm²/C²)
A spring is stretched by 5 cm by a force 10 N. The time period of the oscillations when a mass of 2 kg is suspended by it is:
questions.topic: Time period of a spring-mass system

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed v and the remaining distance with speed 2v. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal distances traveled at different speeds = 2v1v2/(v1+v2) = 2(v)(2v)/(v+2v) = 4v²/3v = 4v/3.

questions.text: The interaction energy of London force is inversely proportional to the sixth power of the distance between two interacting particles, but their magnitude depends upon
options: strength of permanent dipoles in the particles.
questions.explanation: London (dispersion) forces arise from instantaneous induced dipoles, and their strength depends on how easily the electron cloud of a particle can be distorted — i.e., its polarisability.

questions.text: Elimination reaction of 2-Bromo-pentane to form pent-2-ene is: (a) β-Elimination reaction, (b) Follows Zaitsev rule, (c) Dehydrohalogenation reaction, (d) Dehydration reaction
questions.explanation: The elimination of HBr from 2-bromopentane to form the more substituted alkene (pent-2-ene) is a β-elimination (dehydrohalogenation) reaction that follows Zaitsev's rule (more substituted/stable alkene is the major product). Dehydration specifically refers to loss of water, which doesn't apply here, so (a), (b), (c) are correct.

questions.text: If the mass of the Sun were ten times smaller and the universal gravitational constant were ten times larger in magnitude, which of the following is not correct?
options: 'g' on the Earth will not change.
Time period of a simple pendulum on the Earth would decrease.
Walking on the ground would become more difficult.
questions.topic: Effect of scaling solar mass and gravitational constant
questions.explanation: g on Earth = GM_earth/R_earth², which depends on G and Earth's mass (not the Sun's mass). Since G is increased by 10 times, g on Earth would actually increase (not remain unchanged), making this statement not correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cristae, (b) Thylakoids, (c) Centromere, (d) Cisternae with (i) Primary constriction in chromosome, (ii) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus, (iii) Infoldings in mitochondria, (iv) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids.
questions.explanation: Cristae are infoldings in mitochondria (iii); Thylakoids are membranous sacs in plastid stroma (iv); Centromere is the primary constriction in chromosome (i); Cisternae are disc-shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: Identify the type of flowers based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium with respect to the ovary from the given figures (a) and (b) [Figure: two flower longitudinal sections showing different ovary positions]
questions.topic: Flower Types - Perigynous vs Epigynous Identification from Figure
questions.explanation: Based on the figure, both flower (a) and flower (b) show the perigynous condition, where the ovary is in the centre and other floral parts arise from the rim of a cup-shaped thalamus at the same level. 11th NCERT Page No. 62.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements about Histones is Wrong?
options: Histones carry positive charge in the side chain.
Histones are organized to form a unit of 8 molecules.
The pH of histones is slightly acidic.
Histones are rich in amino acids - Lysine and Arginine.
questions.explanation: Histones are basic proteins (not acidic) due to their richness in basic amino acids lysine and arginine, which carry positive charges. The statement that histones have slightly acidic pH is wrong.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Phase of cell cycle) — A. G1 phase, B. S phase, C. G2 phase, D. M phase. List II (Activity) — I. Actual cell division occurs, II. Cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA, III. Synthesis of DNA occurs and the amount of DNA per cell doubles, IV. Proteins are synthesised while cell growth continues.
questions.topic: Matching cell cycle phase to activity
questions.explanation: G1: cell grows, metabolically active, no DNA replication (II); S phase: DNA synthesis/doubling (III); G2: protein synthesis continues, cell prepares for division (IV); M phase: actual division (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: You measure two quantities as A = 1.0 m ± 0.2 m, B = 2.0 m ± 0.2 m. We should report correct value for √(AB) as:
Consider the following reaction and identify the product (P). 3-Methylbutan-2-ol (CH3-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH3) reacts with HBr to give Product (P).
questions.topic: Reaction of Alcohols with HBr (SN1 with Rearrangement)
questions.explanation: HBr protonates the OH to form a secondary carbocation after loss of water. This secondary carbocation undergoes a hydride (H-) shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation, which is then attacked by Br- to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product (P), via the classic SN1 rearrangement pathway.

questions.text: Correct increasing order for the wavelengths of absorption in the visible region for the complexes of Co3+ is:
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength is en > NH3 > H2O, so the crystal field splitting energy (and thus absorbed photon energy) follows [Co(en)3]3+ > [Co(NH3)6]3+ > [Co(H2O)6]3+. Since wavelength is inversely proportional to energy, the increasing order of absorption wavelength is [Co(H2O)6]3+ < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(en)3]3+.

questions.text: An electron is moving in a circular path under the influence of a transverse magnetic field of 3.57×10⁻² T. If the value of e/m is 1.76×10¹¹ C/kg, the frequency of revolution of the electron is:
questions.topic: Electron in Circular Magnetic Field - Frequency

questions.text: The extent of physisorption of a gas increases with
options: a decrease in the surface area of the adsorbent.
a decrease in the strength of van der Waals forces.
questions.explanation: Physisorption is an exothermic process governed by weak van der Waals forces, so by Le Chatelier's principle, lowering the temperature favours and increases the extent of physisorption.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Protoplast fusion, (b) Plant tissue culture, (c) Meristem culture, (d) Micropropagation with (i) Totipotency, (ii) Pomato, (iii) Somaclones, (iv) Virus free plants.
questions.topic: Matching plant biotechnology term to application
questions.explanation: Protoplast fusion gives hybrids like Pomato (ii); Plant tissue culture is based on totipotency (i); Meristem culture gives virus-free plants (iv); Micropropagation produces somaclones (iii). (a)-(ii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is:
questions.explanation: Metamers are ethers (or similar compounds) with the same functional group but different alkyl groups on either side; CH3OCH2CH2CH3 and CH3CH2OCH2CH3 are both ethers with different alkyl distribution — metamers.

questions.text: Given below are half cell reactions: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E(Mn2+/MnO4-) standard = -1.510 V; (1/2)O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E(O2/H2O) standard = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E(cell) = E(cathode, reduction MnO4- to Mn2+) + E(anode, oxidation of H2O to O2) = 1.510 + (-1.223) = 0.287 V. Since E(cell) is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will indeed liberate O2 from water in acidic medium.

questions.text: A specific recognition sequence identified by endonucleases to make cuts at specific positions within the DNA is:
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases recognize specific palindromic nucleotide sequences in DNA and cut at those specific positions.

questions.text: A thick current carrying cable of radius 'R' carries current 'I' uniformly distributed across its cross section. The variation of magnetic field B(r) due to the cable with the distance 'r' from the axis of the cable is represented by:
options: A curve that rises steeply then flattens (concave down, increasing)
A curve that rises slowly then steepens (concave up, increasing)
A straight line through origin with constant positive slope
A curve rising linearly to a peak at r=R then decreasing (1/r dependence beyond)
questions.topic: Magnetic Field Variation in a Thick Current-Carrying Cable
questions.explanation: Inside the cable, Bin = μ0Ir/2πR² (linearly increasing with r). Outside, B0 = μ0I/2πr (decreasing as 1/r). So the field rises linearly to a maximum at r=R (the surface) then decreases as 1/r outside.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 14 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Which of the following diatomic molecular species has only pi bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
questions.explanation: C2 has 12 electrons with configuration sigma1s^2 sigma*1s^2 sigma2s^2 sigma*2s^2 pi2px^2=pi2py^2. Bond order = (8-4)/2 = 2, and both bonds are pi bonds (the last 4 electrons are in pi2px^2 = pi2py^2 orbitals), with no sigma bond from 2p orbitals.

questions.text: For a radioactive material, half-life is 10 minutes. If initially there are 600 number of nuclei, the time taken (in minutes) for the disintegration of 450 nuclei is
questions.explanation: After disintegration of 450 nuclei, 150 nuclei remain out of 600, which is 1/4 of the original. Since (1/2)^n = 1/4 requires n=2 half-lives, time = 2×10 = 20 minutes.

questions.text: Mendel's law of independent assortment holds good for genes situated on
questions.topic: Scope of the Law of Independent Assortment
questions.explanation: Independent assortment applies to genes located on different (non-homologous) chromosomes, which separate into gametes independently of one another; genes on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together (linked) instead.

questions.text: A body weighs 72 N on the surface of the earth. What is the gravitational force on it, at a height equal to half the radius of the earth?
questions.topic: Variation of gravitational force with height

questions.text: Ionized hydrogen atoms and alpha-particles with same momenta enters perpendicular to a constant magnetic field B. The ratio of their radii of their paths rH : r(alpha) will be:
questions.topic: Motion of Charged Particle in Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: r = mv/qB, so for same momentum (mv), r is proportional to 1/q. Hydrogen ion has charge e, alpha particle has charge 2e. rH = 1/e (in relative units), r_alpha = 1/2e. rH/r_alpha = 2e/e = 2:1.

questions.text: The process of appearance of recombination nodules occurs at which sub stage of prophase I in meiosis?
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules, the sites of crossing over, appear during the pachytene substage of prophase I in meiosis.

questions.text: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% into light. If energy of one photon is 4.42×10⁻¹⁹ J, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
questions.topic: Photons emitted per second by a bulb

questions.text: Match Column-I and Column-II and choose the correct match from the given choices. Column-I: (A) Root mean square speed of gas molecules (B) Pressure exerted by ideal gas (C) Average kinetic energy of a molecule (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole of a diatomic gas. Column-II: (P) (1/3)nmv̄² (Q) √(3RT/M) (R) (5/2)RT (S) (3/2)kBT
questions.topic: RMS Speed, Pressure, Kinetic Energy, Internal Energy
questions.explanation: Vrms = √(3RT/M) → A-Q. P = (1/3)nmVm² → B-P. Average KE = (3/2)kT → C-S. Total internal energy of diatomic gas = (5/2)RT → D-R.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Modern Homo sapiens arose in Australia and moved across continents.
Statement II: Homo sapiens arose around 75000 to 10000 years ago.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Modern Homo sapiens arose in AFRICA (not Australia) and then spread/moved across other continents (the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis) -- Statement I is incorrect. As per the standard NCERT account, Homo sapiens arose approximately 75,000 to 10,000 years ago -- Statement II is correct as per this textbook figure.

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.explanation: The two equal-mass fragments (mass 2m/5 each) have momenta (2m/5)v perpendicular to each other, so their resultant momentum is sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v. By conservation of momentum (initial momentum zero), the third fragment (mass m/5) must have equal and opposite momentum: (m/5)*v3 = sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v, giving v3 = 2*sqrt(2)*v.

questions.text: When initial concentration of the reactant is doubled, the half-life period of a zero order reaction
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, t1/2 = [A]0/(2k), which is directly proportional to the initial concentration. Doubling [A]0 doubles the half-life.

questions.text: The strong reducing behaviour of H3PO2 (hypophosphorous acid) is due to
options: the low oxidation state of phosphorus.
the presence of two –OH groups and one P–H bond.
the presence of one –OH group and two P–H bonds.
the high electron gain enthalpy of phosphorus.
questions.topic: Structural Basis of H3PO2's Strong Reducing Behaviour
questions.explanation: Hypophosphorous acid has the structure with one P–OH group and two P–H bonds. The two easily oxidisable P–H bonds are responsible for its strong reducing character, not a low oxidation state of P (which is actually +1, a relatively high state for phosphorus's reduced acids) or electron gain enthalpy.

questions.text: Pinus seed cannot germinate and establish without fungal association. This is because:
options: It has very hard seed coat
Its seeds contain inhibitors that prevent germination.
It has obligate association with mycorrhizae.
questions.explanation: Pinus has an obligate association with mycorrhizal fungi, which is necessary for seed germination and establishment of the seedling.

questions.text: Due to increasing air borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to:
options: Proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls
reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes
benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity
questions.explanation: Wheezing due to air borne allergens and pollutants in urban areas is caused by inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles, a characteristic feature of asthma.

questions.text: 500 mL of 5M solution is diluted to 1500 mL. What is the molarity of resulting solution?
Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p=total pressure of gaseous mixture.
options: pi = xi*p, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = xi*p1°, where xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, p1° = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
questions.explanation: Option (3) is not a correct form of Dalton's Law - the equation pi = xi*p1° does not represent Dalton's law of partial pressure correctly (the terms as defined don't form a valid relationship). Options 1, 2, and 4 are all valid forms of Dalton's law.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is [Given pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57+1 = 5.57.

questions.text: If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.
questions.topic: Dimensions of energy from F, A, T
questions.explanation: Energy=Force×distance; distance=½AT². So Energy=F×A T²/2, dimensionally [F][A][T²].

questions.text:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Solanaceae family?
(a) Flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic
(b) Calyx have five sepals and are united
(c) Androecium have five stamens and are epipetalous
(d) Ovary is inferior
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In Solanaceae, flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic (regular) -- (a) correct. The calyx has five sepals, gamosepalous (united) -- (b) correct. The androecium has five stamens, epipetalous (attached to the petals) -- (c) correct. The ovary in Solanaceae is SUPERIOR, not inferior -- (d) is incorrect. So (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: A linear aperture whose width is 0.02 cm is placed immediately in front of a lens of focal length 60 cm. The aperture is illuminated normally by a parallel beam of wavelength 5×10⁻⁵ cm. The distance of the first dark band of the diffraction pattern from the centre of the screen is:
questions.explanation: For single-slit diffraction, the first dark fringe position is y = λD/d, where D is the focal length (distance to screen) and d is the slit width. Substituting d=0.02 cm, λ=5×10⁻⁵ cm, D=60 cm: y = (5×10⁻⁵ × 60)/0.02 = 0.15 cm.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 15 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A light ray enters through a right angled prism at point P with the angle of incidence 30° as shown in figure. It travels through the prism parallel to its base BC and emerges along the face AC. The refractive index of the prism is: [Figure: right-angled prism ABC with right angle at A, ray entering at P on AB with 30° incidence, traveling parallel to BC, emerging at AC]
questions.topic: Refractive Index of Right-Angled Prism from Ray Geometry
questions.explanation: For AB surface: sin30° = μsin(90°-C), so 1/2 = μcosC ...(i). For AC surface (critical angle, grazing emergence): μsinC = 1, so μ = 1/sinC ...(ii). Substituting (ii) into (i): 1/2 = cosC/sinC, so tanC = 2, giving sinC = 2/√5. From (ii): μ = 1/(2/√5) = √5/2.

questions.text: Sweet potato and potato represent a certain type of evolution. Select the correct combination of terms to explain the evolution
questions.topic: Analogous Organs - Convergent Evolution (Sweet Potato & Potato)
questions.explanation: Sweet potato (modified root) and potato (modified stem) perform a similar function (storage) but have different origins - this is analogy, resulting from convergent evolution. Class 11th NCERT Page No.115.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed/naked, both before and after fertilization. Class 11th NCERT Page No 34.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement from the following:
options: Wrought iron is impure iron with 4% carbon.
Blister copper has blistered appearance due to evolution of CO2.
Vapour phase refining is carried out for Nickel by Van Arkel method.
Pig iron can be moulded into a variety of shapes.
questions.topic: Properties of iron and copper metallurgy
questions.explanation: Pig iron, obtained directly from the blast furnace, is impure but can be cast into various shapes (cast iron), making this the correct statement; wrought iron has very low (not 4%) carbon, blister copper's appearance is due to evolution of SO2 (not CO2), and Nickel is purified by the Mond process (not Van Arkel, which is used for Ti/Zr).

questions.text: Among eukaryotes, replication of DNA takes place in:
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs during the S (synthesis) phase of interphase in the eukaryotic cell cycle.

questions.text: A capillary tube of radius r is immersed in water and water rises in it to a height h. The mass of the water in the capillary is 5 g. Another capillary tube of radius 2r is immersed in water. The mass of water that will rise in this tube is:
questions.topic: Capillary rise and mass of water
questions.explanation: Mass of water risen = ρ×πr²×h. Since h ∝ 1/r (capillary rise), mass ∝ r²×(1/r) = r. Doubling the radius doubles the mass: 5×2 = 10 g.

questions.text: In a vernier calipers, (N+1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is:
questions.explanation: L.C. = 1MSD × (b-a)/b where b=N+1 vernier divisions, a=N main divisions. 1MSD = 0.1mm = 0.1/10 cm = 1/100 cm. L.C. = [((N+1)-N)/(N+1)] × 1/100 = 1/(100(N+1)) cm.

questions.text: The structure of intermediate A in the following reaction is: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) + O2 -> A, then A + H+/H2O -> Phenol + Acetone
options: Phenyl-O-O-CH(CH3)-CH3 structure (isopropyl peroxide attached via O-O to phenyl ring at CH)
questions.explanation: In the cumene process, cumene reacts with O2 to form cumene hydroperoxide (intermediate A), where the tertiary C-H of the isopropyl group is converted to C-O-O-H. Acid hydrolysis of cumene hydroperoxide then gives phenol and acetone.

questions.text: In calcium fluoride, having the fluorite structure, the coordination numbers for calcium ion (Ca2+) and fluoride ion (F-) are:
questions.explanation: In CaF2 fluorite structure, Ca2+ has coordination number 8 and F- has coordination number 4, giving ratio 8:4

questions.text: Hormones are called chemical signals that stimulate specific target tissues. Which of the following is the correct location of the receptors in the case of protein hormones?
questions.explanation: Protein hormones, being large and unable to cross the lipid bilayer, bind to receptors located on the plasma membrane of target cells, unlike steroid/thyroid hormones, which have intracellular or nuclear receptors.

questions.text: Regarding cross-linked or network polymers, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: They contain covalent bonds between various linear polymer chains.
They contain strong covalent bonds in their polymer chains.
They are formed from bi- and tri-functional monomers.
questions.explanation: All polymer chains, whether cross-linked or not, contain strong covalent bonds within the chain; this statement does not distinguish or correctly characterise cross-linked/network polymers specifically, making it the incorrect statement among the options describing their defining branching/cross-linking nature.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In an equilibrium mixture of ice and water kept in a perfectly insulated flask, the mass of ice and water does not change with time.
The intensity of red colour increases when oxalic acid is added to a solution containing iron (III) nitrate and potassium thiocyanate.
On addition of a catalyst, the equilibrium constant value is not affected.
Equilibrium constant for a reaction with a negative ΔH value decreases as the temperature increases.
questions.topic: Le Chatelier's Principle and Equilibrium Shifts
questions.explanation: Oxalic acid reacts with Fe³⁺ ions, removing free Fe³⁺ from the equilibrium Fe³⁺ + SCN⁻ ⇌ [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ (red). Removing Fe³⁺ shifts equilibrium backward, decreasing (not increasing) the intensity of the red colour — making this statement incorrect.

questions.text: Calculate the maximum acceleration of a moving car so that a body lying on the floor of the car remains stationary. The coefficient of static friction between the body and the floor is 0.15 (g=10 ms^-2).
questions.explanation: For the body to remain stationary, the pseudo force must not exceed the maximum static friction: ma_max = μmg, so a_max = μg = 0.15×10 = 1.5 m/s².

questions.text: The mean length of an object is 5 cm. Which of the following measurements is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Accuracy refers to closeness to the true/mean value while maintaining a precision level consistent with the given mean. 4.9 cm is closest to the mean value of 5 cm without implying false extra precision.

questions.text: Good vision depends on adequate intake of carotene-rich food. Select the best option from the following statements: (a) Vitamin A derivatives are formed from carotene. (b) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment. (c) Retinal is a derivative of Vitamin A. (d) Retinal is a light absorbing part of all the visual photopigments.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (c), and (d) are correct: Vitamin A derivatives form from carotene, retinal is a Vitamin A derivative, and retinal is the light-absorbing component of all visual photopigments. Statement (b) is incorrect because photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the outer segment, not the inner segment, of photoreceptor cells.

questions.text: Two Polaroids P₁ and P₂ are placed with their axis perpendicular to each other. Unpolarised light I₀ is incident on P₁. A third polaroid P₃ is kept in between P₁ and P₂ such that its axis makes an angle 45° with that of P₁. The intensity of transmitted light through P₂ is:
questions.explanation: After P₁: I₁ = I₀/2. After P₃ (45° to P₁): I₂ = I₁cos²45° = (I₀/2)(1/2) = I₀/4. After P₂ (45° to P₃, since P₂ is perpendicular to P₁): I₃ = I₂cos²45° = (I₀/4)(1/2) = I₀/8.

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of a particle and its associated momentum (p) is:
options: A straight line with negative slope
A hyperbola-like decreasing curve (λ decreasing as p increases, asymptotic to axes)
A straight line with positive slope
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength vs Momentum Graph
questions.explanation: According to de Broglie, λ = h/p, so λ ∝ 1/p. This relation is a hyperbola, i.e., λ decreases as p increases, asymptotic to both axes.

questions.text: The transfer of genetic material from one bacterium to another through the mediation of a vector like a virus is termed
questions.explanation: Transduction is the process by which a bacteriophage (virus) acts as a vector, transferring genetic material from one bacterium to another, distinct from conjugation (direct cell-to-cell transfer) or transformation (uptake of free DNA from the environment).

questions.text: Which statement about the ozone hole is correct?
options: It is a hole in the stratosphere through which ozone oozes out.
It is a hole in the troposphere through which ozone oozes out.
It is the thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer at some places.
It is the complete vanishing of the ozone layer around the earth.
questions.explanation: The 'ozone hole' is not a literal hole but refers to significant thinning (depletion) of the stratospheric ozone layer over specific regions, particularly over Antarctica.

questions.text: The relation between n_m (n_m = the number of permissible values of magnetic quantum number m) for a given value of azimuthal quantum number (l), is:
questions.explanation: For a given azimuthal quantum number l, the magnetic quantum number m takes values from -l to +l, giving a total of (2l+1) permissible values. So n_m = 2l+1, which rearranges to l = (n_m - 1)/2.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 16 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Select the correct statements from the following: (A) Atoms of all elements are composed of two fundamental particles. (B) The mass of the electron is 9.10939 x 10^-31 kg. (C) All the isotopes of a given element show same chemical properties. (D) Protons and electrons are collectively known as nucleons. (E) Dalton's atomic theory regarded the atom as an ultimate particle of matter. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement A is incorrect — atoms are composed of three fundamental particles (electron, proton, neutron), not two. Statement B is correct — the mass of the electron is 9.10939 x 10^-31 kg. Statement C is correct — isotopes have the same number of electrons/protons, so they show the same chemical properties. Statement D is incorrect — protons and neutrons (not electrons) are collectively known as nucleons. Statement E is correct — Dalton's atomic theory regarded the atom as an indivisible, ultimate particle of matter. So B, C, and E are correct.

questions.text: The appearance of recombination nodules on homologous chromosomes during meiosis characterizes:
options: Sites at which crossing over occurs
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules are structures that appear on the synaptonemal complex during pachytene stage of meiosis I, marking the sites at which crossing over occurs between homologous chromosomes.

questions.text: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time t, then variation of the photocurrent I and magnitude of the stopping potential |V| with time is best represented by:
options: I decreases linearly with t, and |V| also decreases linearly with t
I stays constant (flat) with t, and |V| decreases linearly with t
I stays constant (flat) with t, and |V| also stays constant (flat) with t
I decreases linearly with t, and |V| stays constant (flat) with t
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect - Current and Stopping Potential vs Time
questions.explanation: Photocurrent is proportional to the intensity (power) of light, so as power decreases linearly with time, photocurrent I also decreases linearly. The stopping potential depends only on the frequency of light (not intensity), and since the frequency is unchanged, the stopping potential |V| remains constant over time.

questions.text: The solids which have the negative temperature coefficient of resistance are:
questions.explanation: Both insulators and semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient of resistance, as their resistance decreases with increasing temperature due to more charge carriers becoming available, unlike metals whose resistance increases with temperature.

questions.text: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) for Ne2 is:
questions.explanation: Ne2 (hypothetical) would have 20 electrons total (10 from each Ne atom), completely filling all 10 molecular orbitals formed from 1s and 2s/2p atomic orbitals: σ1s, σ*1s, σ2s, σ*2s, σ2pz, π2px, π2py, π*2px, π*2py, σ*2pz. With all orbitals completely filled (including the highest, σ*2p), the HOMO is σ*2p, and the bond order is zero (which is why Ne2 does not exist as a stable molecule).

questions.text: Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as "Universal recipients". This is due to:
options: Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
Presence of antibodies anti-A and anti-B on RBCs
questions.explanation: AB blood group individuals lack both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma, so they can receive blood from any ABO group without agglutination reaction, making them universal recipients.

questions.text: Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length f each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is F1. When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerin (which has the same refractive index (mu=1.5) as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is F2. The ratio F1:F2 will be:
questions.explanation: For two lenses in contact: feq = f/2, so F1 = f/2. When glycerin (same refractive index as glass) fills the space, it forms a plano-concave lens of negligible effect since glycerin has the same refractive index as the lens glass, so the equivalent system behaves like a single lens of focal length f, so F2 = f. F1:F2 = (f/2):f = 1:2.

questions.text: An increase in the concentration of the reactants of a reaction leads to change in:
questions.topic: Effect of concentration on rate (collision theory)
questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of reactants increases the number of molecules per unit volume, leading to a higher collision frequency between reacting molecules, which increases the rate of reaction, without changing activation energy, threshold energy, or heat of reaction.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]²⁺ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]²⁺ and (C) [Ni(en)3]²⁺ is
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O; as en content increases, crystal field splitting energy increases: (C) > (A) > (B).

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Pyridine (nitrogen in aromatic ring) (2) Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) (3) Azobenzene (benzene-N=N-benzene) (4) Nitrobenzene (benzene with NO2 group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method is not applicable to nitrogen present in nitro and azo groups, or nitrogen present in a ring (like pyridine). It works for aniline, where the NH2 group nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulphate.

questions.text: The temperature of a metallic sphere of radius R is increased by a small amount ΔT. If the linear coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal is α, the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere is:
questions.topic: Thermal Expansion - Volume Expansion of a Sphere
questions.explanation: Volume V = (4/3)πR³. Differentiating: dV = 4πR² dR. Using linear expansion dR = RαΔT, we get dV = 4πR²(RαΔT) = 4πR³αΔT.

questions.text: How many plants among Indigofera, Sesbania, Salvia, Allium, Aloe, mustard, groundnut, radish, gram and turnip have stamens with different lengths in their flowers?
questions.explanation: Four of the listed plants (e.g. mustard - tetradynamous, Salvia - didynamous type arrangements) show stamens of different lengths (heteromorphic stamens) in their flowers.

questions.text: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for extracting energy from carbohydrates to form ATP?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion is the site of cellular respiration, where energy stored in carbohydrates (and other food molecules) is extracted and converted into ATP, the cell's usable energy currency.

questions.text: Match the following concerning essential elements and their functions in plants: (a) Iron, (b) Zinc, (c) Boron, (d) Manganese with (i) Photolysis of water, (ii) Pollen germination, (iii) Required for chlorophyll biosynthesis, (iv) IAA biosynthesis
questions.topic: Functions of essential elements in plants
questions.explanation: Iron is required for chlorophyll biosynthesis (iii), Zinc is needed for IAA (auxin) biosynthesis (iv), Boron is important for pollen germination (ii), and Manganese is involved in the photolysis of water (i). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: In a potentiometer circuit a cell of EMF 1.5 V gives balance point at 36 cm length of wire. If another cell of EMF 2.5 V replaces the first cell, then at what length of the wire, the balance point occurs?
questions.explanation: Balance length ∝ EMF. L2=L1×(E2/E1)=36×(2.5/1.5)=60 cm.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistances P and Q:
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum sensitivity and precision in a Wheatstone bridge, the resistances P and Q should be approximately equal to each other (and to X and Y) and relatively small, to minimize measurement error from galvanometer sensitivity.

questions.text: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 25 degrees C is 0.0210 ohm^-1 cm^-1 and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 25 degrees C is 60 ohm. The value of cell constant is:
questions.explanation: Cell constant G* = Conductivity (K) x Resistance (R) = 0.0210 ohm^-1cm^-1 x 60 ohm = 1.26 cm^-1.

questions.text: Measuring Zeta potential is useful in determining which property of colloidal solution?
questions.explanation: Zeta potential is a measure of the electrostatic charge/potential at the slipping plane of colloidal particles, which determines the degree of repulsion between particles and hence the stability of the colloidal dispersion.

questions.text: Two identical bodies are made of a material for which the heat capacity increases with temperature. One of these is at 100°C, while the other one is at 0°C. If the two bodies are brought into contact, then, assuming no heat loss, the final common temperature is:
questions.explanation: Since heat capacity increases with temperature, the hotter body (100°C) has a higher heat capacity, so it loses less temperature change for the same heat transferred compared to the colder body gaining; the equilibrium temperature shifts closer to the hotter body's value, making it more than 50°C.

questions.text: Genes R and Y follow independent assortment. If RRYY produce round yellow seeds and rryy produce wrinkled green seeds, what will be the phenotypic ratio of the F2 generation?
questions.topic: Dihybrid Cross - Phenotypic Ratio in F2
questions.explanation: In a dihybrid cross following independent assortment, the F2 generation shows round-yellow : round-green : wrinkled-yellow : wrinkled-green phenotypes in the ratio 9:3:3:1. Class 12th NCERT Page No.64.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 17 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct about viroids?
options: They have RNA with protein coat.
They have free RNA without protein coat.
They have DNA with protein coat.
They have free DNA without protein coat.
questions.explanation: Viroids, discovered by T.O. Diener, are infectious agents smaller than viruses, consisting of free RNA (low molecular weight) without any protein coat, unlike viruses which have a protein coat surrounding their nucleic acid.

questions.text: A satellite is orbiting just above the surface of the earth with period T. If d is the density of the earth and G is the universal constant of gravitation, the quantity 3π/(Gd) represents:
questions.topic: Satellite Orbital Period and Earth Density
questions.explanation: For a satellite orbiting just above Earth's surface, T² = 4π²R³/(GM). Substituting M = (4/3)πR³d: T² = 4π²R³/(G×(4/3)πR³d) = 3π/(Gd).

questions.text: Electrophilic addition reactions proceed in two steps. The first step involves the addition of an electrophile. Name the type of intermediate formed in the first step of the following addition reaction: H3C-HC=CH2 + H+ → ?
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule, H+ adds to the terminal (less substituted) carbon of propene, generating the more stable secondary (2°) carbocation on the middle carbon: CH3-CH+-CH3.

questions.text: Plants which produce characteristic pneumatophores and show vivipary belong to:
questions.explanation: Halophytes, such as mangrove plants growing in saline swampy habitats, produce special breathing roots called pneumatophores and exhibit vivipary (seed germination while still attached to the parent plant).

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair - lone pair' electron repulsions?
questions.topic: Lone Pair-Lone Pair Repulsions in Molecules
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom (trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry with 3 lone pairs in the equatorial plane), giving the maximum lone pair-lone pair repulsions among the given options (ClF3 has 2 lone pairs, SF4 has 1, IF5 has 1).

questions.text: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power (p) and magnification (m) for each lens will be, respectively -
questions.explanation: For lenses in contact, net power Pnet = P1+P2+P3+P4 = 4P. Total magnification is the product of individual magnifications: mtotal = m×m×m×m = m⁴.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not correct?
options: Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum
The hydrolytic enzymes of lysosomes are active under acidic pH
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the GOLGI APPARATUS, not the endoplasmic reticulum. This makes statement 2 incorrect.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes: (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (C) [Ni(en)3]2+ is:
questions.explanation: The energy absorbed (v abs) is proportional to the ligand field strength. Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than water. More en ligands means stronger field and higher energy absorption. So [Ni(en)3]2+ (C, 3 en) > [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (A, 2 en) > [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (B, 1 en).

questions.text: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to
options: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
√2 times the rms value of the ac source
