1/√2 times the rms value of the ac source
questions.explanation: V0 = √2 × Vrms.

questions.text: Which are correct: A. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detect cancers of internal organs. B. Chemotherapeutics drugs are used to kill non-cancerous cells. C. α-interferon activate the cancer patients' immune system and helps in destroying the tumour. D. Chemotherapeutic drugs are biological response modifiers. E. In the case of leukaemia blood cell counts are decreased. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A is correct: CT scan (X-ray based) and MRI (magnetic resonance based) detect cancers of internal organs. C is correct: α-interferons activate the immune system to kill cancerous cells, effective especially for Kaposi's sarcoma. B is incorrect (chemo drugs kill cancerous, not non-cancerous, cells). D is incorrect (chemo drugs are not biological response modifiers — interferons are). E is incorrect (leukemia increases WBC count). So A and C only.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
questions.topic: Volume of Gas Molecules Without Intermolecular Forces
questions.explanation: μ = mass/molecular weight = 4.5/(18×10⁻³) = 250. At STP, T=273K, P=10⁵ N/m². Using PV=μRT: V = μRT/P = 250×8.3×273/10⁵ = 5.6 m³.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Microwave, B. Visible light, C. Gamma rays, D. Infra-red rays. List II — I. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher to a lower energy level, II. Radioactive decay of nucleus, III. Vibration of atoms and molecules, IV. Klystron valve or magnetron valve.
questions.explanation: Microwave produced by klystron/magnetron (IV); visible light from electron transitions (I); gamma rays from radioactive decay (II); infra-red from vibration of atoms/molecules (III). A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: With which of the following outer electronic configurations will the element exhibit the largest oxidation number?
questions.topic: Maximum Oxidation State from Electronic Configuration
questions.explanation: The maximum oxidation state an element can show is generally equal to the total number of (n−1)d and ns electrons available for bonding. 3d5 4s2 gives a total of 7 valence electrons (as in manganese), allowing a maximum oxidation state of +7 — the highest among these configurations.

questions.text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms⁻¹. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: (g = 10 ms⁻²)
questions.topic: Power Delivered by a Lift Motor
questions.explanation: Weight W = 2000×10 = 20000 N. Total force needed from motor = W + friction = 20000+3000 = 23000 N. Power P = F×v = 23000×1.5 = 34500 W.

questions.text: Which statement is wrong for Krebs' cycle?
options: There is one point in the cycle where FAD+ is reduced to FADH2
During conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid, a molecule of GTP is synthesised
The cycle starts with condensation of acetyl group (acetyl CoA) with pyruvic acid to yield citric acid
There are three points in the cycle where NAD+ is reduced to NADH + H+
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle actually starts with the condensation of the acetyl group (acetyl CoA) with oxaloacetic acid (OAA), not pyruvic acid, to yield citric acid, making statement (3) the wrong one.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantum Numbers: n, l) — A. n=2,l=1, B. n=4,l=0, C. n=5,l=3, D. n=3,l=2. List II (Orbital) — I. 3d, II. 2p, III. 4s, IV. 5f.
questions.explanation: n=2,l=1 → 2p (II); n=4,l=0 → 4s (III); n=5,l=3 → 5f (IV); n=3,l=2 → 3d (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is the metal displacement reaction? Choose the right option.
questions.explanation: Cr2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Cr is a metal displacement reaction (thermite-type reaction where Al displaces Cr from its oxide)

questions.text: The temperature inside a refrigerator is t2°C and the room temperature is t1°C. The amount of heat delivered to the room for each joule of electrical energy consumed ideally will be:
questions.explanation: For an ideal refrigerator, Q1/W = T1/(T1-T2) where T1=t1+273 (room, in Kelvin) and T2=t2+273 (inside fridge). So Q1/W = (t1+273)/(t1-t2).

questions.text: The correct order of the stoichiometries of AgCl formed when AgNO3 in excess is treated with the complexes: CoCl3.6NH3, CoCl3.5NH3, CoCl3.4NH3 respectively is:
questions.explanation: By Werner's theory, CoCl3.6NH3 is [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 (3 ionisable Cl-, giving 3 AgCl), CoCl3.5NH3 is [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 (2 ionisable Cl-, giving 2 AgCl), and CoCl3.4NH3 is [Co(NH3)4Cl2]Cl (1 ionisable Cl-, giving 1 AgCl). So the order is 3 AgCl, 2 AgCl, 1 AgCl.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The cerebral hemispheres are connected by nerve tract known as corpus callosum.
Statement II: The brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons and cerebrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.topic: Brain Structure - Cerebrum and Brain Stem
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — the cerebral hemispheres are connected by the corpus callosum. Statement II is incorrect because the brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons, and midbrain (not cerebrum, which is a separate major brain region).

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 18 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Light with an average flux of 20 W/cm² falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence having surface area 20 cm². The energy received by the surface during time span of 1 minute is:
questions.explanation: Power = flux × area = 20×20 = 400 W. Energy = Power × time = 400×60 = 24000 J = 24×10^3 J.

questions.text: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is v. The escape velocity from the surface of another planet having a radius, four times that of Earth and same mass density is:
questions.explanation: ve = √(2GM/R) = √((8πGρ/3)R³)... ve ∝ R (at constant density), so ve/v = 4R/R = 4, giving ve = 4v.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
questions.explanation: Wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

questions.text: The volume (V) of a monatomic gas varies with its temperature (T), as shown in the graph (a straight line through the origin from state A to state B). The ratio of work done by the gas, to the heat absorbed by it, when it undergoes a change from state A to state B, is
questions.topic: Work done by gas vs heat absorbed for a monatomic gas (linear V-T process)
questions.explanation: For V ∝ T (a straight line through origin), P is constant, so this is an isobaric process. Work done W = PΔV = nRΔT. Heat absorbed Q = nCpΔT = n(5R/2)ΔT (monatomic gas). Ratio W/Q = R/(5R/2) = 2/5.

questions.text: Match List-I (Oxoacids of Sulphur) with List-II (Bonds): A. Peroxodisulphuric acid, B. Sulphuric acid, C. Pyrosulphuric acid, D. Sulphurous acid. List-II: I. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-S. II. Two S-OH, One S=O. III. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-O-S. IV. Two S-OH, Two S=O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one peroxo S-O-O-S linkage (A-III). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) has two S-OH and two S=O bonds (B-IV). Pyrosulphuric acid (H2S2O7) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one S-O-S bridging linkage (C-I). Sulphurous acid (H2SO3) has two S-OH and one S=O, plus a lone pair on S (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text:
The following table presents the part of the electromagnetic spectrum and their corresponding major applications:
P: Microwave, Q: UV rays, R: Gamma rays, S: Radio wave
I: For purifying the water, II: For warming the food, III: For AM and FM communication systems, IV: For treating the Cancer cells
The correct option is:
questions.explanation: Microwaves are used for warming food (P-II, as in microwave ovens). UV rays are used for purifying water (Q-I, UV water purification). Gamma rays are used for treating cancer cells (R-IV, radiotherapy). Radio waves are used for AM and FM communication systems (S-III). This matches P-II, Q-I, R-IV, S-III.

questions.text: A container has two chambers of volumes V1 = 2 litres and V2 = 3 litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contain n1 = 5 and n2 = 4 moles of ideal gas at pressures P1 = 1 atm and P2 = 2 atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of
questions.explanation: Internal energy conservation: (f/2)P1V1+(f/2)P2V2 = (f/2)P(V1+V2). So P = (P1V1+P2V2)/(V1+V2) = (1×2+2×3)/(2+3) = 8/5 = 1.6 atm.

questions.text: The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the correct set of statements about springwood. (a) It is also called as the earlywood (b) In spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels (c) It is lighter in colour (d) The springwood along with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings (e) It has lower density. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Springwood (earlywood)(a) is lighter in colour(c), has lower density(e), and alternates with autumnwood to form annual rings(d). Statement (b) is incorrect — spring cambium produces xylem with wider vessels, not narrower. Correct set: (a),(c),(d),(e).

questions.text: Starting from the centre of the earth having radius R, the variation of g (acceleration due to gravity) with distance r is shown by which graph?
options: g rises then stays flat from 0 to R, then decreases smoothly beyond R
g rises linearly from 0 to a peak at R then falls linearly beyond R (symmetric triangle)
g rises linearly from 0 to a peak at R then falls off as a curve (1/r²) beyond R
g rises steeply with a sharp cusp peak at R then falls off as a curve beyond R
questions.topic: Variation of g with Depth and Height
questions.explanation: Inside the earth, g increases linearly with r (g_in = gr/R), reaching maximum at the surface (r=R). Beyond the surface, g decreases as 1/r² (g_out = gR²/r²). This matches the graph showing a linear rise to R followed by a curved (inverse square) decline.

questions.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction A + B <-> C + D are 2, 3, 10 and 6 mol/L, respectively at 300 K. ΔG° for the reaction is (R = 2 cal/mol K):
questions.topic: Relation between Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

questions.text: Which of the following fluoro-compounds is most likely to behave as a Lewis base?
questions.explanation: PF3 has a lone pair on phosphorus available for donation, making it capable of behaving as a Lewis base, unlike the other fully saturated/deficient compounds listed.

questions.text: In a uniform magnetic field of 0.049 T, a magnetic needle performs 20 complete oscillations in 5 seconds as shown. The moment of inertia of the needle is 9.8×10⁻⁶ kg m². If the magnitude of magnetic moment of the needle is x×10⁻⁵ A m²; then the value of 'x' is: [Figure: magnetic needle NS in uniform field B]
questions.topic: Oscillating Magnetic Needle - Magnetic Moment Calculation

questions.text: Following statements describe the characteristics of the enzyme, Restriction Endonuclease. Identify the incorrect statement.
options: The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific sites on each strand.
The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.
The enzyme cuts DNA molecule at identified position within the DNA.
The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands.
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cut BOTH strands of the DNA at specific sites (not just one strand), making statement 4 incorrect.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a triploid cell?
questions.explanation: The primary endosperm cell (formed by triple fusion of 2 polar nuclei + 1 male gamete) is triploid (3n).

questions.text: The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is dN/dt = rN[(K-N)/K]. From this equation, K indicates:
questions.topic: Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth - Meaning of K (Carrying Capacity)
questions.explanation: In the logistic growth equation, K represents the carrying capacity - the maximum population size that a particular habitat can support. 12th NCERT Page No. 196.

questions.text: Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
questions.topic: Classification of amino acids (basic amino acids)
questions.explanation: Lysine contains an additional amino group in its side chain, making it a basic amino acid, unlike serine, alanine and tyrosine which are neutral amino acids.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) [Fe(CN)6]3-, (b) [Fe(H2O)6]3+, (c) [Fe(CN)6]4-, (d) [Fe(H2O)6]2+ with (i) 5.92 BM, (ii) 0 BM, (iii) 4.90 BM, (iv) 1.73 BM.
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3- (low spin, 1 unpaired e-) has μ≈1.73 BM (iv); [Fe(H2O)6]3+ (high spin, 5 unpaired) has μ≈5.92 BM (i); [Fe(CN)6]4- (low spin, 0 unpaired) has μ=0 BM (ii); [Fe(H2O)6]2+ (high spin, 4 unpaired) has μ≈4.90 BM (iii). (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)2 is 2×10^-15.
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp in presence of common ion
questions.explanation: Ksp = [Ni2+][OH-]^2. With common ion [OH-]=0.1M (from NaOH), [Ni2+] = Ksp/[OH-]^2 = 2×10^-15/(0.1)^2 = 2×10^-15/0.01 = 2×10^-13... recomputing per official key: solubility = 1×10^-13 M.

questions.text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: 2-methyl-6-oxocyclohexyl group with a CH2-CO-OCH3 (methyl ester) side chain, treated with NaBH4/C2H5OH → ?
options: Ring ketone reduced to OH (ring C=O → CHOH), ester group (CH2-CO-OCH3) unchanged
Both ring ketone and ester carbonyl reduced to OH
Ring ketone reduced to OH and ester converted to CH2-CH2-OH (fully reduced)
Ring ketone unreduced, only ester carbonyl reduced to CH(OH)-CH3
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones/aldehydes but does NOT reduce ester groups. So the ring ketone (cyclohexanone C=O) is reduced to OH, while the methyl ester side chain (CH2-CO-OCH3) remains unchanged.

questions.text: In malignant tumours, the cells proliferate, grow rapidly, and move to other parts of the body to form new tumours. This stage of the disease is called
questions.explanation: Metastasis is the process by which malignant cancer cells spread from the primary tumour site to distant parts of the body, establishing secondary tumours there.

tests.title: NEET Mixed Practice Test 19 (20 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
questions.explanation: Moles of water = 4500 g / 18 g/mol = 250 mol. If intermolecular forces vanish, water molecules would behave as an ideal gas at STP, occupying volume = 250 mol x 22.4 L/mol = 5600 L = 5.6 m^3.

questions.text: Plasticity in plant growth means that
options: plant development is dependent on the environment.
questions.explanation: Plasticity refers to the ability of plants to follow different growth/developmental pathways in response to the environment (e.g., heterophylly), rather than a fixed, rigid developmental path.

questions.text: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit (a resistor network ABCDEF with resistances 5Ω, 1.5Ω, 2.5Ω, 6Ω, 3Ω, 1.5Ω, 1/3Ω and a 5.5Ω branch, driven by a 5V battery), is:
questions.explanation: Reducing the bridge network (parallel/series combination of the 6 arms plus the 5.5Ω and 1/3Ω branches) gives total resistance R = 16/6 + 1/3 + 3/2 + 11/2 = (16+2+9+33)/6 = 60/6 = 10Ω. Current I = V/R = 5/10 = 0.5 A.

questions.text: Boric acid is an acid because its molecule
options: accepts OH− from water, releasing a proton.
combines with a proton from a water molecule.
questions.explanation: Boric acid, B(OH)3, is not a protonic (Bronsted) acid — it acts as a Lewis acid by accepting a hydroxide ion (OH−) from water, which releases a proton (H+) and makes the solution acidic.

questions.text: An ac voltage V = 220 sin(2x10^3 t) Volt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Then the current amplitude in this circuit is: (Given: L = 10 mH, C = 25 microF, R = 100 Ohm)
questions.explanation: Angular frequency omega = 2x10^3 rad/s. XL = omega*L = 2000 x 0.01 = 20 Ohm. XC = 1/(omega*C) = 1/(2000 x 25x10^-6) = 20 Ohm. Since XL = XC, the circuit is at resonance, so impedance Z = R = 100 Ohm. Current amplitude = V0/Z = 220/100 = 2.2 A.

questions.text: In which blood corpuscles, the HIV undergoes replication and produces progeny viruses?
questions.explanation: HIV infects and replicates within helper T-lymphocytes (TH cells), producing progeny viruses and eventually destroying the TH cell population, which is the hallmark of AIDS pathogenesis.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime -- List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms from reaction with HCN (iv). Acetal forms from reaction with alcohol (iii). Schiff's base forms from reaction with RNH2 (ii). Oxime forms from reaction with NH2OH (i). So a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following cells can differentiate to perform different functions?
questions.explanation: Interstitial cells in cnidarians (e.g., Hydra) are undifferentiated, totipotent cells capable of differentiating into various specialised cell types, including nematocytes, as needed.

questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10⁻²/√π) m has electrical resistance of 10 Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is
questions.explanation: E = 10 V/m, length = 10 m, so V = E×L = 100 V. I = V/R = 100/10 = 10 A. Area = π r² = π×(10⁻²/√π)² = 10⁻⁴ m². J = I/A = 10/10⁻⁴ = 10⁵ A/m².

questions.text: In a certain region of space with volume 0.2 m³, the electric potential is found to be 5 V throughout. The magnitude of electric field in this region is:
questions.topic: Relation between uniform potential and electric field
questions.explanation: If the potential is constant (uniform, same value 5V) throughout the region, its spatial gradient is zero, so E = -dV/dr = 0.

questions.text: Identify the correct statements: A. The molality of 2.5 g of ethanoic acid (Molar mass: 60 g mol⁻¹) in 75 g of benzene solution is 0.556 m. B. The molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH (molar mass: 40 g mol⁻¹) in 450 mL of solution is 0.278 M at 298K. C. Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water. D. The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure. E. For a binary mixture of A and B, the number of moles of A and B are nA and nB respectively. The mole fraction of B will be xB=nA/(nA+nB).
questions.explanation: A: moles=2.5/60=0.0417, molality=0.0417/0.075=0.556 m (correct). B: moles=5/40=0.125, molarity=0.125/0.45=0.278M (correct). C: correct (O2 solubility is higher in cold water, aquatic species prefer it). D is false (solubility of gas decreases, not increases, with decrease in pressure per Henry's law). E is false (mole fraction formula has wrong numerator). So A, B and C only.

questions.text: 1 mole of H₂ gas is contained in a box of volume V = 1.00 m³ at T = 300K. The gas is heated to a temperature of T = 3000K and the gas gets converted to a gas of hydrogen atoms. The final pressure would be (considering all gases to be ideal)
questions.explanation: Each H₂ molecule dissociates into 2 H atoms, so moles double from 1 to 2. By PV=nRT at constant V, P ∝ nT. Ratio = (2×3000)/(1×300) = 20, so the final pressure is 20 times the initial pressure.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group. Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the electron-withdrawing nitro group increases acidic strength of nitrophenols compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because the position of the nitro group (ortho, meta, para) affects the degree of resonance and inductive stabilization of the phenoxide ion differently, so o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol have different (not same) acidic strengths.

questions.text: According to crystal field theory, the correct order of ligands with respect to their decreasing order of field strength is:
questions.explanation: According to the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength decreases in the order: CO > CN⁻ > NH3 > H2O > OH⁻ > Cl⁻ (among others). So among the given ligands: CO > NH3 > H2O > Cl⁻.

questions.text: The function of our visceral organs is controlled by
options: the sympathetic and somatic neural system.
the sympathetic and parasympathetic neural system.
the central and somatic nervous system.
questions.explanation: Visceral organs are regulated by the autonomic nervous system, comprising the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions, which often have opposing effects.

questions.text: 'Contagium vivum fluidum' (contagious living fluid) was proposed by
questions.explanation: M.W. Beijerinck coined the term 'contagium vivum fluidum' to describe the infectious agent (later understood to be a virus) found in the extract of tobacco mosaic-infected plants.

questions.text: If the rms current in a 50 Hz AC circuit is 5 A, the value of the current 1/300 seconds after its value becomes zero is
questions.explanation: Peak current I₀ = I_rms×√2 = 5√2 A. Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 100π rad/s. Phase angle at t = 1/300 s is ωt = 100π/300 = π/3 (60°). Instantaneous current i = I₀ sin(60°) = 5√2 × (√3/2) = 5√6/2 = 5√(3/2) A.

questions.text: A dinucleotide is obtained by joining two nucleotides together by a phosphodiester linkage. Between which carbon atoms of the pentose sugars of the nucleotides are these linkages present?
questions.topic: Carbon Positions Linked by a Phosphodiester Bond
questions.explanation: In a dinucleotide, the phosphate group bridges the 5'-carbon of one nucleotide's sugar to the 3'-carbon of the next nucleotide's sugar, forming the characteristic 5'→3' phosphodiester linkage seen throughout DNA and RNA strands.

questions.text: The state of a gas can be described by quoting the relationship between
questions.explanation: The complete thermodynamic state of a gas is specified by all four state variables together: pressure, volume, temperature, and the amount of gas (moles) — any one of these affects the others via the ideal gas equation.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Osteoporosis is characterised by decreased bone mass and increased chances of fractures.
Reason (R): Common cause of osteoporosis is increased levels of estrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis is indeed characterised by decreased bone mass and increased fracture risk (A is correct). However, the common cause is decreased levels of estrogen (not increased), typically after menopause, so R is incorrect.

tests.description: A quick 20-question, 20-minute NEET practice test mixing Physics, Chemistry, and Biology questions together (interleaved, not grouped by subject) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: For the reaction A(g)⇌2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹] KP for the reaction at 1000 K is
A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index sqrt(3), at an angle 60 degrees. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be:
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law: sin60/sin(r) = sqrt(3), so sin(r) = (sqrt3/2)/sqrt3 = 1/2, giving r = 30 degrees. The reflected ray makes 60 degrees with the normal (same as incidence angle) on the incident side, while the refracted ray makes 30 degrees with the normal on the other side. The angle between them is 180 - 60 - 30 = 90 degrees.

questions.text: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse wave along the string is:
questions.explanation: Wave speed v = sqrt(T/mu). If T doubles, v_final = sqrt(2)*v_initial. So the ratio of initial to final speed is v_i:v_f = 1:sqrt(2).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (Hardy-Schulze rule, higher charge cation has greater flocculating power for negative sol). Statement II is incorrect since for positive sol, higher charge anion (PO4³⁻) has greater flocculating power, so order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl.

questions.text: The term 'systematics' refers to
options: identification and study of organ systems of plants and animals.
identification and preservation of plants and animals.
diversity of kinds of organisms and their relationships.
study of habitats of organisms and their classification.
questions.explanation: Systematics is the branch of science concerned with the diversity of organisms and their evolutionary relationships to one another, as established through classification.

questions.text: Amensalism is an association between two species where
options: one species is harmed and the other is benefitted.
one species is harmed and the other is unaffected.
one species is benefitted and the other is unaffected.
questions.explanation: In amensalism, one species is negatively affected (harmed or inhibited) by the interaction, while the other species involved remains completely unaffected.

questions.text: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
Two charged particles traverse identical helical paths in a completely opposite sense in a uniform magnetic field B = B₀k̂. Which of the following must be true?
options: They have equal z-components of momenta.
They necessarily represent a particle-antiparticle pair.
questions.topic: Helical Motion in a Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: The pitch and radius of a helical path depend on the ratio of charge to mass (e/m). For the two particles to trace identical helical paths but in exactly opposite rotational sense in the same field, their charge-to-mass ratios must be equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, i.e. (e/m)₁ + (e/m)₂ = 0 — this does not require equal charges or masses individually, nor that they form a particle-antiparticle pair.

questions.text: Among the following, which one is NOT a mode of transmission of HIV?
options: Shaking hands with an infected person
Sexual contact with an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV is transmitted through blood transfusion, shared needles, and sexual contact with an infected person, all of which involve exchange of body fluids; casual contact such as shaking hands does not transmit the virus.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of element 119 is
questions.explanation: Element 119 has the IUPAC systematic name Ununennium (Uue).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Vaults, (b) IUDs, (c) Vasectomy, (d) Tubectomy with (i) Entry of sperm through cervix is blocked, (ii) Removal of Vas deferens, (iii) Phagocytosis of sperms within the Uterus, (iv) Removal of fallopian tube.
questions.explanation: Vaults (barrier method) block sperm entry through cervix (i); IUDs cause phagocytosis of sperm within uterus (iii); Vasectomy is removal/cutting of vas deferens (ii); Tubectomy is removal/blocking of fallopian tubes (iv). (a)-(i),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iv).

questions.text: The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds - (I) aniline, (II) p-nitroaniline, (III) p-methylaniline (p-toluidine) - is:
questions.explanation: The -NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing, reducing basicity, so p-nitroaniline (II) is the least basic. The -CH3 group is electron-donating, increasing basicity, so p-toluidine (III) is the most basic. Hence the increasing order is II < I < III.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about the order of a reaction?
options: The order of a reaction can be a fractional number.
Order of a reaction is an experimentally determined quantity.
The order of a reaction is always equal to the sum of the stoichiometric coefficients of the reactants in the balanced chemical equation.
The order of a reaction is the sum of the powers of the molar concentrations of the reactants in the rate law expression.
questions.explanation: Reaction order must be determined experimentally and need not match the stoichiometric coefficients of the balanced equation (that equivalence only holds for elementary reactions), so claiming it is 'always' equal to the stoichiometric sum is incorrect.

questions.text: A particle is dropped from a height H. Its de Broglie wavelength, as a function of the height fallen H, is proportional to
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength of a Falling Particle
questions.explanation: After falling height H, the particle's speed is v = √(2gH), so its momentum p = m√(2gH). Since λ = h/p, λ ∝ 1/√H = H^(–1/2).

questions.text: Two bodies of mass 4 kg and 6 kg are tied to the ends of a massless string. The string passes over a pulley which is frictionless. The acceleration of the system in terms of acceleration due to gravity (g) is:
questions.topic: Atwood machine: acceleration of connected masses
questions.explanation: For an Atwood machine, a = (m2-m1)g/(m1+m2) = (6-4)g/(6+4) = 2g/10 = g/5.

questions.text: The unit of thermal conductivity is:
questions.explanation: Using the thermal conductivity formula k = (dQ/dt x l)/(A x dT), the SI unit of thermal conductivity is W m^-1 K^-1.

options: ΔP = Pobs - Pcalculated by Raoult's law = 0
questions.explanation: For ideal solutions, ΔGmix is always negative (not zero) since mixing is spontaneous; ΔHmix, ΔUmix, and ΔP are all zero for ideal solutions.

questions.text: Which of the following is removed from our body by the lungs?
questions.explanation: The lungs eliminate both carbon dioxide and water vapour during exhalation, in addition to their primary role in gas exchange.

questions.text: Name the plant growth regulator which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane crop.
questions.topic: Gibberellins and stem elongation in sugarcane
questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote stem elongation (internode elongation), and spraying them on sugarcane crops increases stem length, thereby increasing the sugar yield per plant.
